    raise NotImplementedError("milestone 10: format_command")
--- solution
"""A key-value store with a write-ahead log, crash recovery and a query language.

The layers, from the bottom up:

  records      the binary record: length, CRC32 checksum, sequence number
  MemFS        a simulated file system that can crash after any byte
  KVStore      an in-memory table, made durable by a write-ahead log
  SSTable      a sorted, immutable file with an index
  SkipList     the sorted in-memory table, for range scans
  LSM tree     the memtable flushes to SSTables listed in a manifest
  compaction   many SSTables merged into one
  Transaction  writes that become durable together, or not at all
  queries      a tokenizer and parser for PUT, GET, DEL, SCAN, COUNT, ...
"""
from bisect import bisect_right
import hashlib
import difflib
import heapq
import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import NamedTuple


# ===========================================================================
# Records
# ===========================================================================
# Every file this store writes is made of records. On disk, one record is:
#
#     length   u32   how many bytes the body has
#     crc      u32   zlib.crc32 of the body
#     body:
#       seq    u64   sequence number: 1, 2, 3, ... in the order written
#       kind   u8    what the record does: PUT, DELETE, ...
#       klen   u32   length of the key in bytes (UTF-8)
#       vlen   u32   length of the value in bytes (UTF-8)
#       key    klen bytes
#       value  vlen bytes
#
# All integers are little-endian ("<" in struct).

HEADER = struct.Struct("<II")    # length, crc
BODY = struct.Struct("<QBII")    # seq, kind, klen, vlen
MAX_BODY = 1 << 24               # 16 MiB: a longer body is damage, not data

PUT = 1
DELETE = 2
BEGIN = 3
COMMIT = 4
KINDS = {PUT, DELETE, BEGIN, COMMIT}


class Record(NamedTuple):
    seq: int
    kind: int
    key: str
    value: str = ""


class RecordError(Exception):
    """The bytes at an offset are not one whole, valid record."""


class TornRecord(RecordError):
    """The data ends before the record does: the last write was cut short."""


class CorruptRecord(RecordError):
    """All of the record's bytes are there, but they are damaged."""


def encode_record(record):
    """The bytes of one record: the header, then the body."""
    key = record.key.encode("utf-8")
    value = record.value.encode("utf-8")
    body = BODY.pack(record.seq, record.kind, len(key), len(value)) + key + value
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY:
        # Never write what decode_record would reject: it would be lost.
        raise ValueError(f"record of {len(body)} bytes is larger than {MAX_BODY}")
    return HEADER.pack(len(body), zlib.crc32(body)) + body


def decode_record(data, offset=0):
    """Decode the record that starts at data[offset].

    Returns (record, end), where end is the offset just past the record.
    Raises TornRecord if the data stops before the record ends, and
    CorruptRecord if the record is complete but fails a check.
    """
    left = len(data) - offset
    if left < HEADER.size:
        raise TornRecord(f"offset {offset}: {left} of {HEADER.size} header bytes")
    length, crc = HEADER.unpack_from(data, offset)
    if length < BODY.size or length > MAX_BODY:
        raise CorruptRecord(f"offset {offset}: impossible body length {length}")
    start = offset + HEADER.size
    end = start + length
    if end > len(data):
        raise TornRecord(f"offset {offset}: body of {length} bytes, {len(data) - start} there")
    body = bytes(data[start:end])
    if zlib.crc32(body) != crc:
        raise CorruptRecord(f"offset {offset}: checksum mismatch")
    seq, kind, klen, vlen = BODY.unpack_from(body)
    if kind not in KINDS:
        raise CorruptRecord(f"offset {offset}: unknown kind {kind}")
    if BODY.size + klen + vlen != length:
        raise CorruptRecord(f"offset {offset}: key and value lengths do not add up")
    try:
        key = body[BODY.size:BODY.size + klen].decode("utf-8")
        value = body[BODY.size + klen:].decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise CorruptRecord(f"offset {offset}: text is not valid UTF-8") from None
    return Record(seq, kind, key, value), end


def read_records(data):
    """Decode records from the start of data, stopping at the first bad one.

    Returns (records, good_end, problem). good_end is the offset just past
    the last good record. problem is None when all of data was good, "torn"
    when it ends in a cut-off record, and "corrupt" when a record is damaged.
    """
    records = []
    offset = 0
    while offset < len(data):
        try:
            record, end = decode_record(data, offset)
        except TornRecord:
            return records, offset, "torn"
        except CorruptRecord:
            return records, offset, "corrupt"
        records.append(record)
        offset = end
    return records, offset, None


# ===========================================================================
# A file system that can crash
# ===========================================================================
class SimulatedCrash(Exception):
    """The simulated machine died in the middle of an operation.

    Store code must never catch this: a real crash cannot be caught either.
    """


class MemFS:
    """An in-memory file system that can crash after any byte.

    Every byte written is one step, and so is each sync, rename, truncate
    and delete. With budget=k exactly k steps happen: the machine crashes
    when step k + 1 is tried, part-way through a write if need be.
    budget=None never crashes. `steps` counts the steps taken, so one run
    with no budget measures a workload.

    The program sees every byte it has written. crash() gives the files a
    restarted machine finds: every written byte after a process crash, only
    the synced bytes after a power loss.
    """

    def __init__(self, budget=None):
        self.files = {}      # name -> bytearray: what the program sees
        self.synced = {}     # name -> how many leading bytes are durable
        self.budget = budget
        self.steps = 0
        self.crashed = False

    # -- the crash machinery ------------------------------------------------

    def _allow(self, n):
        """Take up to n steps; return how many the budget allows."""
        if self.crashed:
            raise SimulatedCrash("the machine has already crashed")
        if self.budget is None:
            allowed = n
        else:
            allowed = max(0, min(n, self.budget - self.steps))
        self.steps += allowed
        return allowed

    def _die(self):
        self.crashed = True
        raise SimulatedCrash(f"crashed after {self.steps} steps")

    def _step(self):
        if self._allow(1) < 1:
            self._die()

    def _need(self, name):
        if name not in self.files:
            raise FileNotFoundError(name)

    # -- reading costs no steps --------------------------------------------

    def exists(self, name):
        return name in self.files

    def names(self):
        return sorted(self.files)

    def size(self, name):
        self._need(name)
        return len(self.files[name])

    def read(self, name):
        self._need(name)
        return bytes(self.files[name])

    def read_at(self, name, offset, size):
        """Up to size bytes from offset on (fewer at the end of the file)."""
        self._need(name)
        return bytes(self.files[name][offset:offset + size])

    # -- writing: every byte and every operation is a step -----------------

    def append(self, name, data):
        """Add bytes to the end of a file, creating it if needed."""
        allowed = self._allow(len(data))
        if name not in self.files:
            self.files[name] = bytearray()
            self.synced[name] = 0
        self.files[name] += data[:allowed]
        if allowed < len(data):
            self._die()

    def sync(self, name):
        """Make every byte written to the file so far durable (fsync)."""
        self._need(name)
        self._step()
        self.synced[name] = len(self.files[name])

    def rename(self, old, new):
        """Give a file a new name in one atomic step, replacing any file there."""
        self._need(old)
        self._step()
        self.files[new] = self.files.pop(old)
        self.synced[new] = self.synced.pop(old)

    def truncate(self, name, size):
        """Cut a file down to its first size bytes."""
        self._need(name)
        if not 0 <= size <= len(self.files[name]):
            raise ValueError(f"cannot truncate {name} to {size} bytes")
        self._step()
        del self.files[name][size:]
        self.synced[name] = min(self.synced[name], size)

    def delete(self, name):
        self._need(name)
        self._step()
        del self.files[name]
        del self.synced[name]

    # -- crashing -------------------------------------------------------------

    def crash(self, power_loss=False):
        """The files a restarted machine finds, as a new MemFS with no budget."""
        after = MemFS()
        for name, data in self.files.items():
            keep = self.synced[name] if power_loss else len(data)
            after.files[name] = bytearray(data[:keep])
            after.synced[name] = keep
        return after

    def listing(self):
        """One line per file: name, size, and how much of it is synced."""
        return "\n".join(f"{name}  {len(self.files[name])} bytes, {self.synced[name]} synced"
                         for name in self.names())

    def __repr__(self):
        state = "crashed" if self.crashed else f"{self.steps} steps"
        return f"<MemFS {len(self.files)} files, {state}>"

    def attempt(self, fn):
        """Run fn(). True if it finished, False if this file system crashed."""
        try:
            fn()
        except SimulatedCrash:
            if not self.crashed:
                raise
        return not self.crashed


def append_record(fs, name, record):
    """Append one record to a log file and make it durable."""
    fs.append(name, encode_record(record))
    fs.sync(name)


def load_records(fs, name):
    """The good records at the start of a log file ([] if there is no file)."""
    if not fs.exists(name):
        return []
    return read_records(fs.read(name))[0]


KIND_NAMES = {PUT: "PUT", DELETE: "DELETE"}
KIND_NAMES.update({BEGIN: "BEGIN", COMMIT: "COMMIT"})


def describe_log(data):
    """A listing of log bytes for people debugging: one line per record with
    its offset, sequence number, kind, key and value, then what (if
    anything) is wrong with the tail."""
    lines = []
    offset = 0
    while offset < len(data):
        try:
            record, end = decode_record(data, offset)
        except TornRecord:
            lines.append(f"{offset:>6}  torn: {len(data) - offset} bytes not used")
            break
        except CorruptRecord:
            lines.append(f"{offset:>6}  corrupt: {len(data) - offset} bytes not used")
            break
        text = f"{offset:>6}  #{record.seq} {KIND_NAMES[record.kind]}"
        if record.key:
            text += f" {record.key!r}"
        if record.kind == PUT:
            text += f" = {record.value!r}"
        lines.append(text)
        offset = end
    return "\n".join(lines)


def write_atomically(fs, name, data):
    """Write a whole file so that `name` is either untouched or complete.

    The bytes go to a temporary file, which is synced, then renamed over
    `name`. A crash at any step leaves the old file (or none) in place.
    """
    tmp = name + ".tmp"
    if fs.exists(tmp):
        fs.delete(tmp)      # left over from a write that crashed
    fs.append(tmp, data)
    fs.sync(tmp)            # durable before it gets the real name
    fs.rename(tmp, name)


# ===========================================================================
# SSTables: sorted, immutable files with an index
# ===========================================================================
# Costs, for n entries and an index of every B-th key: opening a table
# reads the footer and n/B index keys; get does a binary search of the
# index, O(log(n/B)) comparisons, then decodes at most B entries; a scan
# of m entries decodes about m + B. The file never changes after it is
# written, so it needs no locking and can be copied or cached freely.
#
# An SSTable holds entries in key order, each one a record (PUT, or DELETE
# for a tombstone), then a sparse index, then a fixed-size footer:
#
#     data     entry 0, entry 1, ..., entry n-1
#     index    for every index_every-th entry: u32 key length, key, u64 offset
#     bloom    the Bloom filter's bit array
#     footer   magic b"KVSST002", u64 index offset, u64 index entries,
#              u64 entry count, u64 seq, u32 crc32 of the index,
#              u64 bloom offset, u32 bloom bits, u32 bloom hashes,
#              u32 crc32 of the bloom, u32 crc32 of the footer before it

SST_MAGIC = b"KVSST002"
SST_FOOTER = struct.Struct("<8sQQQQIQIIII")
U32 = struct.Struct("<I")
U64 = struct.Struct("<Q")


class BloomFilter:
    """A set that answers "definitely not here" or "probably here".

    It is an array of `bits` bits and `hashes` hash functions. add() sets the
    key's `hashes` bits; a key may be present only if all of its bits are
    set. It never says no to a key that was added. With 10 bits per key and
    7 hashes, about 1 absent key in 100 gets a wrong "probably".
    """

    def __init__(self, bits, hashes, data=None):
        if bits < 1 or hashes < 1:
            raise ValueError("a Bloom filter needs at least one bit and one hash")
        self.bits = bits
        self.hashes = hashes
        self.array = bytearray((bits + 7) // 8) if data is None else bytearray(data)

    @classmethod
    def for_keys(cls, n, bits_per_key=10):
        """A filter sized for n keys: k = bits per key times ln 2 is best."""
        bits = max(64, n * bits_per_key)
        return cls(bits, max(1, round(bits_per_key * 0.69)))

    def _positions(self, key):
        # Double hashing: two 64-bit hashes h1, h2 give the k positions
        # h1 + i*h2, as good as k independent hashes for a Bloom filter.
        digest = hashlib.blake2b(key.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=16).digest()
        h1 = int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "little")
        h2 = int.from_bytes(digest[8:], "little") | 1
        return [(h1 + i * h2) % self.bits for i in range(self.hashes)]

    def add(self, key):
        for p in self._positions(key):
            self.array[p >> 3] |= 1 << (p & 7)

    def __contains__(self, key):
        return all(self.array[p >> 3] & (1 << (p & 7)) for p in self._positions(key))


def write_sstable(fs, name, entries, seq, index_every=16):
    """Write (key, value) entries, in strictly increasing key order, as an
    SSTable. A value of None is a tombstone. The file appears atomically."""
    if index_every < 1:
        raise ValueError("index_every must be at least 1")
    entries = list(entries)
    bloom = BloomFilter.for_keys(len(entries))
    data = bytearray()
    index = bytearray()
    index_count = 0
    count = 0
    previous = None
    for key, value in entries:
        if previous is not None and key <= previous:
            raise ValueError(f"keys must be strictly increasing: {previous!r} then {key!r}")
        previous = key
        if count % index_every == 0:
            raw = key.encode("utf-8")
            index += U32.pack(len(raw)) + raw + U64.pack(len(data))
            index_count += 1
        if value is None:
            data += encode_record(Record(seq, DELETE, key))
        else:
            data += encode_record(Record(seq, PUT, key, value))
        bloom.add(key)
        count += 1
    bits = bytes(bloom.array)
    head = SST_FOOTER.pack(SST_MAGIC, len(data), index_count, count, seq, zlib.crc32(index),
                           len(data) + len(index), bloom.bits, bloom.hashes, zlib.crc32(bits), 0)[:-4]
    footer = head + U32.pack(zlib.crc32(head))
    write_atomically(fs, name, bytes(data + index + bits + footer))


class SSTable:
    """Reads one SSTable file. Only the footer and the index live in memory;
    entries are read from the file when needed."""

    def __init__(self, fs, name):
        self.fs = fs
        self.name = name
        size = fs.size(name)
        if size < SST_FOOTER.size:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{name}: too short to be an SSTable")
        footer = fs.read_at(name, size - SST_FOOTER.size, SST_FOOTER.size)
        (magic, index_at, index_count, count, seq, index_crc,
         bloom_at, bloom_bits, bloom_hashes, bloom_crc, footer_crc) = SST_FOOTER.unpack(footer)
        if magic != SST_MAGIC or zlib.crc32(footer[:-4]) != footer_crc:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{name}: bad footer")
        index_end = bloom_at
        bloom_end = size - SST_FOOTER.size
        if not index_at <= bloom_at <= bloom_end:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{name}: sections out of order")
        bits = fs.read_at(name, bloom_at, bloom_end - bloom_at)
        if zlib.crc32(bits) != bloom_crc or len(bits) != (bloom_bits + 7) // 8:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{name}: bloom filter checksum mismatch")
        self.bloom = BloomFilter(bloom_bits, bloom_hashes, bits)
        if index_at > index_end:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{name}: index offset past the end")
        raw = fs.read_at(name, index_at, index_end - index_at)
        if zlib.crc32(raw) != index_crc:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{name}: index checksum mismatch")
        self.keys = []       # every index_every-th key, in order
        self.offsets = []    # where each of those entries starts
        pos = 0
        for _ in range(index_count):
            (klen,) = U32.unpack_from(raw, pos)
            self.keys.append(raw[pos + 4:pos + 4 + klen].decode("utf-8"))
            (offset,) = U64.unpack_from(raw, pos + 4 + klen)
            self.offsets.append(offset)
            pos += 4 + klen + 8
        self.data_end = index_at
        self.count = count
        self.seq = seq
        self.reads = 0       # entries decoded so far, for tests of the cost
        self.bloom_skips = 0 # gets the Bloom filter answered with no read

    def __len__(self):
        return self.count

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<SSTable {self.name!r}: {self.count} entries, seq {self.seq}>"

    def _entry(self, offset):
        """The entry at offset, and the offset of the next one."""
        head = self.fs.read_at(self.name, offset, HEADER.size)
        if len(head) < HEADER.size or offset + HEADER.size > self.data_end:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{self.name}: entry at {offset} runs past the data")
        (length, _) = HEADER.unpack(head)
        raw = head + self.fs.read_at(self.name, offset + HEADER.size, length)
        try:
            record, size = decode_record(raw)
        except RecordError as error:
            raise CorruptFile(f"{self.name}: {error}") from None
        self.reads += 1
        return record, offset + size

    def _block(self, key):
        """The index slot of the last indexed key <= key (-1 if key is before them all)."""
        return bisect_right(self.keys, key) - 1

    def get(self, key):
        """The entry for key (a PUT or DELETE record), or None if there is none.
        Binary search on the index, then at most one block of entries."""
        if key not in self.bloom:
            self.bloom_skips += 1
            return None                  # definitely not in this table
        slot = self._block(key)
        if slot < 0:
            return None
        offset = self.offsets[slot]
        end = self.offsets[slot + 1] if slot + 1 < len(self.offsets) else self.data_end
        while offset < end:
            record, offset = self._entry(offset)
            if record.key == key:
                return record
            if record.key > key:
                return None
        return None

    def items(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        """(key, value) for every entry with lo <= key < hi, in key order.
        value is None for a tombstone. None for lo or hi means no bound."""
        offset = 0
        if lo is not None and self._block(lo) >= 0:
            offset = self.offsets[self._block(lo)]
        while offset < self.data_end:
            record, offset = self._entry(offset)
            if lo is not None and record.key < lo:
                continue
            if hi is not None and record.key >= hi:
                return
            yield record.key, (record.value if record.kind == PUT else None)


# ===========================================================================
# The skip list: a sorted map in memory
# ===========================================================================
# Costs, for n keys: get, put and delete take O(log n) expected time, since
# each level holds about half the nodes of the one below, so a search makes
# about two moves per level on about log2(n) levels. The random heights
# come from a seeded generator, so a run can be repeated exactly. A scan of
# m keys costs O(log n + m): one search, then a walk along level 0.
class _Node:
    __slots__ = ("key", "value", "next")

    def __init__(self, key, value, height):
        self.key = key
        self.value = value
        self.next = [None] * height    # next[i]: the following node on level i


class SkipList:
    """A sorted map with expected O(log n) get, put and delete.

    Level 0 links every node in key order. Each node also joins level 1
    with probability 1/2, level 2 with probability 1/4, and so on, so a
    search runs along the high levels first and skips most nodes.
    `visits` counts the nodes searches step onto, for tests of the cost.
    """

    MAX_LEVEL = 24

    def __init__(self, seed=0):
        self.head = _Node(None, None, self.MAX_LEVEL)
        self.level = 1       # levels in use
        self.size = 0
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
        self.visits = 0

    def __len__(self):
        return self.size

    def __iter__(self):
        return (key for key, _ in self.items())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<SkipList {self.size} keys, {self.level} levels>"

    def _random_height(self):
        height = 1
        while height < self.MAX_LEVEL and self.rng.random() < 0.5:
            height += 1
        return height

    def _before(self, key):
        """For every level, the last node whose key is less than key."""
        before = [self.head] * self.MAX_LEVEL
        node = self.head
        for level in range(self.level - 1, -1, -1):
            while node.next[level] is not None and node.next[level].key < key:
                node = node.next[level]
                self.visits += 1
            before[level] = node
        return before

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        node = self._before(key)[0].next[0]
        if node is not None and node.key == key:
            return node.value
        return default

    def __contains__(self, key):
        node = self._before(key)[0].next[0]
        return node is not None and node.key == key

    def put(self, key, value):
        """Insert key, or replace its value if it is already there."""
        before = self._before(key)
        node = before[0].next[0]
        if node is not None and node.key == key:
            node.value = value
            return
        height = self._random_height()
        self.level = max(self.level, height)
        node = _Node(key, value, height)
        for level in range(height):
            node.next[level] = before[level].next[level]
            before[level].next[level] = node
        self.size += 1

    def delete(self, key):
        """Remove key. Returns True if it was there."""
        before = self._before(key)
        node = before[0].next[0]
        if node is None or node.key != key:
            return False
        for level in range(len(node.next)):
            before[level].next[level] = node.next[level]
        while self.level > 1 and self.head.next[self.level - 1] is None:
            self.level -= 1
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def check(self):
        """The broken invariants, as a list of text (empty when all is well):
        each level is sorted, each level's nodes are also on the level below,
        and level 0 holds size nodes."""
        problems = []
        below = None
        for level in range(self.level):
            keys = []
            node = self.head.next[level]
            while node is not None:
                keys.append(node.key)
                node = node.next[level]
            if any(a >= b for a, b in zip(keys, keys[1:])):
                problems.append(f"level {level} is not strictly sorted")
            if below is not None and not set(keys) <= below:
                problems.append(f"level {level} has keys missing from level {level - 1}")
            if level == 0 and len(keys) != self.size:
                problems.append(f"level 0 has {len(keys)} nodes, size says {self.size}")
            below = set(keys)
        return problems

    def items(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        """(key, value) pairs with lo <= key < hi, in key order."""
        node = self.head.next[0] if lo is None else self._before(lo)[0].next[0]
        while node is not None and (hi is None or node.key < hi):
            yield node.key, node.value
            node = node.next[0]

    def clear(self):
        """Remove every key. The nodes are taken apart one at a time: in the
        browser, freeing a chain of thousands of nodes in one go overflows
        the stack."""
        node = self.head.next[0]
        self.head = _Node(None, None, self.MAX_LEVEL)
        self.level = 1
        self.size = 0
        while node is not None:
            after = node.next[0]
            node.next = None             # cut this node loose
            node = after


def prefix_end(prefix):
    """The smallest string greater than every string that starts with prefix,
    or None when there is none (the empty prefix, or only U+10FFFF).
    Keys starting with prefix are exactly those with prefix <= key < end."""
    chars = list(prefix)
    while chars:
        last = ord(chars.pop())
        if last < 0x10FFFF:
            chars.append(chr(last + 1))
            return "".join(chars)
    return None


# ===========================================================================
# Merging sorted runs, and the manifest
# ===========================================================================
# The manifest names the SSTables that make up the store, newest first:
#
#     magic   8 bytes  b"KVMAN001"
#     seq     u64      every log record up to seq is in the tables
#     next    u64      the number for the next table file
#     count   u32      how many table names follow
#     names   count times: u32 length, name (UTF-8)
#     crc     u32      zlib.crc32 of every byte before it

MANIFEST_MAGIC = b"KVMAN001"
MANIFEST_HEAD = struct.Struct("<8sQQI")


def encode_manifest(seq, next_table, names):
    out = bytearray(MANIFEST_HEAD.pack(MANIFEST_MAGIC, seq, next_table, len(names)))
    for name in names:
        raw = name.encode("utf-8")
        out += U32.pack(len(raw)) + raw
    out += U32.pack(zlib.crc32(out))
    return bytes(out)


def decode_manifest(data):
    """(seq, next_table, table names) from manifest bytes; CorruptFile if bad."""
    if len(data) < MANIFEST_HEAD.size + 4 or zlib.crc32(data[:-4]) != U32.unpack_from(data, len(data) - 4)[0]:
        raise CorruptFile("manifest checksum mismatch")
    magic, seq, next_table, count = MANIFEST_HEAD.unpack_from(data)
    if magic != MANIFEST_MAGIC:
        raise CorruptFile("not a manifest")
    names = []
    pos = MANIFEST_HEAD.size
    for _ in range(count):
        (length,) = U32.unpack_from(data, pos)
        names.append(data[pos + 4:pos + 4 + length].decode("utf-8"))
        pos += 4 + length
    if pos != len(data) - 4:
        raise CorruptFile("manifest has bytes after its names")
    return seq, next_table, names


def merge_runs(runs):
    """Merge sorted runs of (key, value) pairs, given newest first.

    Yields every key once, in key order, with the value from the newest run
    that has it (None for a tombstone). A heap holds the front pair of each
    run, so k runs with n pairs in all cost O(n log k).
    """
    iterators = [iter(run) for run in runs]
    heap = []

    def push(i):
        pair = next(iterators[i], None)
        if pair is not None:
            heapq.heappush(heap, (pair[0], i, pair[1]))

    for i in range(len(iterators)):
        push(i)
    while heap:
        key, i, value = heapq.heappop(heap)
        push(i)
        while heap and heap[0][0] == key:       # older versions of the same key
            _, j, _ = heapq.heappop(heap)
            push(j)
        yield key, value


# ===========================================================================
# The store
# ===========================================================================
# The invariants that make it correct:
#
#   1. Write-ahead: a record is in the log, and synced, before the memtable
#      changes and before put or delete returns. So every acknowledged
#      write survives a crash, and a crash loses at most the one write that
#      was in flight.
#   2. The log is a clean prefix: recovery replays records while they are
#      whole, checksummed and numbered seq, seq + 1, ... and cuts the log
#      at the first one that is not, so new records never follow garbage.
#   3. Tables plus log: the manifest names the SSTables and the seq they
#      cover; the log holds the records after it (perhaps some before it
#      too, which recovery skips). Files appear whole, because each one is
#      synced under a temporary name and then renamed, and the manifest
#      rename is the single moment a flush or a compaction takes effect.
#   4. Newest wins: the memtable is newer than every table, and tables are
#      kept newest first, so the first layer that has a key decides it. A
#      tombstone (None) in a newer layer hides the key in older ones.
#   5. The oldest table holds no tombstones: there is nothing below it to
#      hide, so a flush onto no tables, or a compaction that includes the
#      oldest table, drops them.
#   6. A transaction's records sit together between BEGIN and COMMIT, and
#      recovery applies them only when the COMMIT is there.


class StoreError(Exception):
    """A request the store cannot carry out."""


class CorruptFile(StoreError):
    """A file that was written whole fails its checks: damage, not a crash."""


class RecoveryReport(NamedTuple):
    replayed: int            # PUT and DELETE records applied from the log
    dropped: int             # bytes cut from the end of the log
    problem: str | None      # why replay stopped early, or None

    def __str__(self):
        text = f"replayed {self.replayed} records"
        if self.problem:
            text += f"; dropped {self.dropped} bytes ({self.problem} tail)"
        return text


def check_key(key):
    if not isinstance(key, str):
        raise TypeError("a key must be a string")
    if not key:
        raise ValueError("a key must not be empty")


def check_value(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise TypeError("a value must be a string")


_MISSING = object()          # "not in this layer", as opposed to a tombstone


class TransactionError(StoreError):
    """A transaction was used after it ended, or no transaction is open."""


class ConflictError(TransactionError):
    """Since the transaction read something, a commit changed it: refused."""


def in_range(key, lo, hi):
    return (lo is None or key >= lo) and (hi is None or key < hi)


class Transaction:
    """Writes that become durable together at commit, or not at all.

    Writes wait in self.writes (key -> value, or None for a delete), and
    reads see them first. commit() logs BEGIN, the writes and COMMIT, and
    syncs once; recovery applies a transaction only if its COMMIT is there.

    Several transactions may be open at once. Each remembers what it read
    from the store (self.reads and self.ranges); commit() first checks that
    all of it is still true, and refuses with ConflictError if another
    commit changed it. This is optimistic concurrency control: no locks,
    and a conflict costs a retry.
    """

    def __init__(self, store):
        self.store = store
        self.writes = {}     # key -> value, or None for a delete
        self.reads = {}      # key -> the value first read from the store
        self.ranges = []     # (lo, hi, pairs first read from the store)
        self.active = True

    def _check(self):
        if not self.active:
            raise TransactionError("the transaction has ended")

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        self._check()
        check_key(key)
        if key in self.writes:
            value = self.writes[key]
        else:
            value = self.store.get(key)
            self.reads.setdefault(key, value)
        return default if value is None else value

    def put(self, key, value):
        self._check()
        check_key(key)
        check_value(value)
        self.writes[key] = value

    def delete(self, key):
        """Delete key at commit. Returns True if the transaction could see it."""
        self._check()
        existed = self.get(key) is not None
        self.writes[key] = None
        return existed

    def scan(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        self._check()
        seen = self.store.scan(lo, hi)
        self.ranges.append((lo, hi, seen))
        mine = sorted((k, v) for k, v in self.writes.items() if in_range(k, lo, hi))
        return [(k, v) for k, v in merge_runs([mine, seen]) if v is not None]

    def count(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        return len(self.scan(lo, hi))

    def conflicts(self):
        """The keys and ranges this transaction read that have changed since."""
        changed = [key for key, value in self.reads.items() if self.store.get(key) != value]
        changed += [(lo, hi) for lo, hi, seen in self.ranges if self.store.scan(lo, hi) != seen]
        return changed

    def commit(self):
        self._check()
        self.active = False
        self.store.open_txns.discard(self)
        changed = self.conflicts()
        if changed:
            raise ConflictError(f"changed since this transaction read them: {changed}")
        self.store._commit(self)

    def abort(self):
        self._check()
        self.active = False
        self.store.open_txns.discard(self)

    # `with store.begin() as txn:` commits at the end of the block, or
    # aborts if the block raises.
    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, kind, error, trace):
        if self.active:
            if kind is None:
                self.commit()
            else:
                self.abort()
        return False


class KVStore:
    """A durable map from non-empty string keys to string values."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        fs,
        name="db",
        wal_limit=None,
        max_tables=None,
        index_every=16,
        seed=0,
    ):
        self.fs = fs
        self.name = name
        self.wal = name + ".wal"
        self.manifest = name + ".manifest"
        self.wal_limit = wal_limit       # checkpoint when the log grows past this
        self.max_tables = max_tables     # compact when there are more tables
        self.index_every = index_every
        self.seed = seed
        self.mem = SkipList(seed)        # key -> value, or None for a tombstone
        self.tables = []                 # open SSTables, newest first
        self.next_table = 1              # number for the next table file
        self.seq = 0                     # sequence number of the last record
        self.checkpoints = 0             # checkpoints taken since opening
        self.compactions = 0             # compactions run since opening
        self.open_txns = set()           # transactions begun and not yet ended
        self.closed = False
        self.recovery = self._recover()

    # -- recovery -------------------------------------------------------------

    def _recover(self):
        """Rebuild the in-memory state from the files, and tidy them."""
        self._load_manifest()
        self._remove_orphans()
        return self._replay_wal()

    def _replay_wal(self):
        """Apply the log to the memtable, stopping at the first bad record.

        A transaction's records wait in `pending` until its COMMIT; if the
        log ends first, they are dropped. The log is then cut back to the
        last point that is safe to append to.
        """
        if not self.fs.exists(self.wal):
            return RecoveryReport(0, 0, None)
        data = self.fs.read(self.wal)
        offset = 0              # end of the last record accepted
        seq = self.seq          # sequence number of that record
        started = False         # past the records the tables already hold?
        pending = None          # records of a transaction not yet committed
        begin_at = 0            # offset of that transaction's BEGIN
        replayed = 0
        problem = None
        while offset < len(data):
            try:
                record, end = decode_record(data, offset)
            except TornRecord:
                problem = "torn"
                break
            except CorruptRecord:
                problem = "corrupt"
                break
            if record.seq <= seq and not started:
                offset = end    # already in the tables
                continue
            if record.seq != seq + 1:
                problem = "gap"
                break
            if record.kind == BEGIN:
                if pending is not None:
                    problem = "corrupt"     # BEGIN inside a transaction
                    break
                pending = []
                begin_at = offset
            elif record.kind == COMMIT:
                if pending is None:
                    problem = "corrupt"     # COMMIT with no BEGIN
                    break
                for op in pending:
                    self._apply(op)
                replayed += len(pending)
                pending = None
            elif pending is not None:
                pending.append(record)
            else:
                self._apply(record)
                replayed += 1
            started = True
            seq = record.seq
            offset = end
            if pending is None:
                self.seq = seq  # only committed records count
        if pending is not None:
            offset = begin_at   # drop the unfinished transaction, BEGIN and all
            problem = problem or "unfinished"
        dropped = len(data) - offset
        if dropped:
            self.fs.truncate(self.wal, offset)
        return RecoveryReport(replayed, dropped, problem)

    def _apply(self, record):
        """Make one PUT or DELETE record true in the memtable."""
        if record.kind == PUT:
            self.mem.put(record.key, record.value)
        else:
            self.mem.put(record.key, None)       # a tombstone hides older tables

    # -- the log ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def _log(self, kind, key="", value=""):
        """Append the next record to the log. Not yet durable: sync after."""
        record = Record(self.seq + 1, kind, key, value)
        self.fs.append(self.wal, encode_record(record))
        self.seq = record.seq
        return record

    def _write(self, kind, key, value=""):
        """Log one record, make it durable, and only then apply it."""
        record = self._log(kind, key, value)
        self.fs.sync(self.wal)
        self._apply(record)
        self._maybe_checkpoint()

    def wal_size(self):
        """How many bytes the log holds."""
        return self.fs.size(self.wal) if self.fs.exists(self.wal) else 0

    def _check_open(self):
        if self.closed:
            raise StoreError("the store is closed")

    # -- reading ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _lookup(self, key):
        """The newest value of key in any layer: None if absent or deleted."""
        value = self.mem.get(key, _MISSING)
        if value is not _MISSING:
            return value
        for table in self.tables:            # newest first: the first hit wins
            record = table.get(key)
            if record is not None:
                return record.value if record.kind == PUT else None
        return None

    def get(self, key, default=None):
        """The value stored under key, or default."""
        self._check_open()
        check_key(key)
        value = self._lookup(key)
        return default if value is None else value

    def __contains__(self, key):
        return self.get(key) is not None

    def _merged(self, lo, hi):
        """Every layer merged: (key, value or None) in key order."""
        runs = [self.mem.items(lo, hi)] + [table.items(lo, hi) for table in self.tables]
        return merge_runs(runs)

    def scan(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        """The live (key, value) pairs with lo <= key < hi, in key order."""
        self._check_open()
        return [(k, v) for k, v in self._merged(lo, hi) if v is not None]

    def count(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        """How many live keys k have lo <= k < hi."""
        self._check_open()
        return sum(1 for _, v in self._merged(lo, hi) if v is not None)

    def items(self):
        return self.scan()

    def keys(self, lo=None, hi=None):
        """The live keys with lo <= key < hi, in key order, one at a time."""
        self._check_open()
        return (k for k, v in self._merged(lo, hi) if v is not None)

    def __iter__(self):
        return self.keys()

    def __len__(self):
        return self.count()

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<KVStore {self.name!r}: seq {self.seq}, {len(self.tables)} tables>"

    # -- writing ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def put(self, key, value):
        """Store value under key. Durable when put returns."""
        self._check_open()
        check_key(key)
        check_value(value)
        self._write(PUT, key, value)

    def delete(self, key):
        """Remove key. Returns True if it was there. Durable when it returns."""
        self._check_open()
        check_key(key)
        if self._lookup(key) is None:
            return False
        self._write(DELETE, key)
        return True

    # -- transactions -------------------------------------------------------------

    def begin(self):
        """Start a transaction."""
        self._check_open()
        txn = Transaction(self)
        self.open_txns.add(txn)
        return txn

    def transact(self, work, attempts=3):
        """Run work(txn) in a transaction and commit it, starting again from
        scratch on a ConflictError, up to `attempts` times. Returns what
        work returned. The usual way to use optimistic transactions."""
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            txn = self.begin()
            try:
                result = work(txn)
            except StoreError:
                if txn.active:
                    txn.abort()
                raise
            if not txn.active:
                return result        # work committed or aborted it itself
            try:
                txn.commit()
                return result
            except ConflictError:
                if attempt == attempts - 1:
                    raise

    def put_many(self, pairs):
        """Store several (key, value) pairs atomically: a crash keeps all or none."""
        with self.begin() as txn:
            for key, value in pairs:
                txn.put(key, value)

    def _commit(self, txn):
        """Log a transaction's writes between BEGIN and COMMIT, sync once, apply."""
        self._check_open()
        ops = [(k, v) for k, v in sorted(txn.writes.items())
               if v is not None or self._lookup(k) is not None]
        if not ops:
            return                          # nothing to make durable
        self._log(BEGIN)
        records = [self._log(PUT, k, v) if v is not None else self._log(DELETE, k) for k, v in ops]
        self._log(COMMIT)
        self.fs.sync(self.wal)              # one sync for the whole transaction
        for record in records:
            self._apply(record)
        self._maybe_checkpoint()

    # -- checkpoints ----------------------------------------------------------------

    def _maybe_checkpoint(self):
        if self.wal_limit is not None and self.wal_size() > self.wal_limit:
            self.checkpoint()

    def _table_name(self, number):
        return f"{self.name}-{number:06d}.sst"

    def checkpoint(self):
        """Flush the memtable to a new SSTable, record it in the manifest, and
        empty the log. Each step is safe to crash in: a table the manifest
        does not name is deleted by recovery, and log records up to the
        manifest's seq are skipped."""
        self._check_open()
        self.checkpoints += 1
        if len(self.mem):
            entries = list(self.mem.items())
            if not self.tables:
                # Nothing older to hide, so tombstones can go.
                entries = [(k, v) for k, v in entries if v is not None]
            name = self._table_name(self.next_table)
            self.next_table += 1
            write_sstable(self.fs, name, entries, self.seq, self.index_every)
            self.tables.insert(0, SSTable(self.fs, name))
        self._save_manifest()
        if self.wal_size():
            self.fs.truncate(self.wal, 0)
        self.mem = SkipList(self.seed)
        self._auto_compact()

    def table_names(self):
        """The SSTable files, newest first."""
        return [table.name for table in self.tables]

    def _save_manifest(self):
        data = encode_manifest(self.seq, self.next_table, self.table_names())
        write_atomically(self.fs, self.manifest, data)

    def _load_manifest(self):
        """Open the tables the manifest names; seq becomes its checkpoint seq."""
        if not self.fs.exists(self.manifest):
            return
        self.seq, self.next_table, names = decode_manifest(self.fs.read(self.manifest))
        self.tables = [SSTable(self.fs, name) for name in names]

    def _remove_orphans(self):
        """Delete files a crash left behind: temporary files, and tables the
        manifest does not name."""
        live = set(self.table_names())
        for name in self.fs.names():
            ours = name.startswith(self.name + "-") and (name.endswith(".sst") or name.endswith(".sst.tmp"))
            if (ours and name not in live) or name == self.manifest + ".tmp":
                self.fs.delete(name)

    def compact(self, count=None):
        """Merge the newest `count` SSTables (all of them by default) into one.

        Only the newest version of each key is kept. Tombstones are dropped
        only when the oldest table is in the merge: otherwise an older table
        may still hold a value that the tombstone must go on hiding. The
        manifest then names the new table in place of the merged ones (one
        atomic rename), and the merged tables are deleted.
        """
        self._check_open()
        count = len(self.tables) if count is None else count
        if not 2 <= count <= len(self.tables):
            return
        merging, older = self.tables[:count], self.tables[count:]
        self.compactions += 1
        entries = list(merge_runs([t.items() for t in merging]))
        if not older:
            entries = [(k, v) for k, v in entries if v is not None]
        merged = []
        if entries:
            name = self._table_name(self.next_table)
            self.next_table += 1
            write_sstable(self.fs, name, entries, merging[0].seq, self.index_every)
            merged = [SSTable(self.fs, name)]
        self.tables = merged + older
        self._save_manifest()                 # the switch: one atomic rename
        for table in merging:
            self.fs.delete(table.name)        # a crash here leaves orphans for recovery

    def _auto_compact(self):
        """Size-tiered compaction, when there are more than max_tables tables.

        Merge the newest tables together, stopping at the first older table
        more than twice as big as all of them so far: small tables get merged
        often, and a big old table is rewritten only when enough has piled up
        on top of it. Rewriting everything every time would cost O(n) per
        flush.
        """
        if self.max_tables is None or len(self.tables) <= self.max_tables:
            return
        count, size = 1, len(self.tables[0])
        while count < len(self.tables) and len(self.tables[count]) <= 2 * size:
            size += len(self.tables[count])
            count += 1
        self.compact(max(count, 2))

    def explain(self, key):
        """How a get of key is answered, layer by layer, as lines of text."""
        self._check_open()
        steps = []
        value = self.mem.get(key, _MISSING)
        if value is not _MISSING:
            return [f"memtable: {'tombstone' if value is None else 'found'}"]
        steps.append("memtable: not there")
        for table in self.tables:
            skips = table.bloom_skips
            record = table.get(key)
            if table.bloom_skips > skips:
                steps.append(f"{table.name}: Bloom filter says no")
            elif record is None:
                steps.append(f"{table.name}: not there (Bloom filter false positive)")
            else:
                steps.append(f"{table.name}: {'found' if record.kind == PUT else 'tombstone'}")
                return steps
        steps.append("not found")
        return steps

    def backup(self, dest):
        """Copy the store into another file system, consistently.

        A checkpoint first moves everything into SSTables. SSTables never
        change once written, so copying them and then the manifest gives a
        store that opens in `dest` with exactly the current contents.
        """
        self.checkpoint()
        for table in self.tables:
            write_atomically(dest, table.name, self.fs.read(table.name))
        write_atomically(dest, self.manifest, self.fs.read(self.manifest))

    def close(self):
        for txn in list(self.open_txns):
            txn.abort()
        self.closed = True


# ===========================================================================
# The query language
# ===========================================================================
#     PUT key value    GET key    DEL key    COUNT prefix
#     SCAN start end   BEGIN      COMMIT     ABORT
#
# A word is a run of characters with no white space and no double quote.
# A quoted string may hold anything, with the escapes \" \\ \n and \t.
# In SCAN, a bare * means "no bound on this side"; the quoted "*" is the key *.
#
# The grammar, in EBNF (keywords may be in any case):
#
#     line     = command { argument } ;       (argument count checked per command)
#     command  = word ;
#     argument = word | string ;
#     word     = char-but-space-or-quote { char-but-space-or-quote } ;
#     string   = '"' { char-but-quote-or-backslash | escape } '"' ;
#     escape   = '\\' ( '"' | '\\' | 'n' | 't' ) ;
#
# Tokenizing is one pass over the line, O(length); so is parsing.


class QueryError(Exception):
    """A line that is not a valid command, and the column where it went wrong."""

    def __init__(self, message, column, line=None):
        where = f"column {column}" if line is None else f"line {line}, column {column}"
        super().__init__(f"{where}: {message}")
        self.message = message
        self.column = column
        self.line = line


class Token(NamedTuple):
    kind: str        # "word" or "string"
    text: str
    column: int      # where the token starts, counting from 1


class Command(NamedTuple):
    op: str          # "PUT", "GET", ...
    args: tuple      # the arguments as strings (None for a bare * in SCAN)


ARGUMENTS = {
    "PUT": ("key", "value"),
    "GET": ("key",),
    "DEL": ("key",),
    "SCAN": ("start", "end"),
    "COUNT": ("prefix",),
    "BEGIN": (),
    "COMMIT": (),
    "ABORT": (),
}
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n", "t": "\t"}


def tokenize(line):
    """Split a line into word and string tokens."""
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(line):
        if line[i].isspace():
            i += 1
        elif line[i] == '"':
            start = i
            i += 1
            chars = []
            while True:
                if i >= len(line):
                    raise QueryError("unterminated string", start + 1)
                ch = line[i]
                if ch == '"':
                    i += 1
                    break
                if ch == "\\":
                    if i + 1 >= len(line):
                        raise QueryError("unterminated string", start + 1)
                    if line[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
                        raise QueryError(f"unknown escape \\{line[i + 1]}", i + 1)
                    chars.append(ESCAPES[line[i + 1]])
                    i += 2
                else:
                    chars.append(ch)
                    i += 1
            if i < len(line) and not line[i].isspace():
                raise QueryError("expected a space after the string", i + 1)
            tokens.append(Token("string", "".join(chars), start + 1))
        else:
            start = i
            while i < len(line) and not line[i].isspace() and line[i] != '"':
                i += 1
            if i < len(line) and line[i] == '"':
                raise QueryError("a quote cannot start inside a word", i + 1)
            tokens.append(Token("word", line[start:i], start + 1))
    return tokens


def parse(line):
    """One line of the query language as a Command; QueryError if it is not one."""
    tokens = tokenize(line)
    if not tokens:
        raise QueryError("empty command", 1)
    first, args = tokens[0], tokens[1:]
    if first.kind != "word":
        raise QueryError("expected a command word", first.column)
    op = first.text.upper()
    if op not in ARGUMENTS:
        message = f"unknown command {first.text!r}"
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(op, ARGUMENTS, n=1)
        if close:
            message += f"; did you mean {close[0]}?"
        raise QueryError(message, first.column)
    names = ARGUMENTS[op]
    if len(args) < len(names):
        raise QueryError(f"{op} is missing the {names[len(args)]}", len(line) + 1)
    if len(args) > len(names):
        raise QueryError(f"too many arguments for {op}", args[len(names)].column)
    values = []
    for name, token in zip(names, args):
        if op == "SCAN" and token.kind == "word" and token.text == "*":
            values.append(None)
        elif name == "key" and token.text == "":
            raise QueryError("the key must not be empty", token.column)
        else:
            values.append(token.text)
    return Command(op, tuple(values))


def script_lines(text):
    """The lines of a script that hold commands: not blank, not # comments."""
    return [line for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.lstrip().startswith("#")]


def parse_script(text):
    """Every command in a script; a QueryError names the line at fault."""
    commands = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        try:
            commands.append(parse(line))
        except QueryError as error:
            raise QueryError(error.message, error.column, number) from None
    return commands


def lint(text):
    """Every error in a script, as text, one per bad line: unlike
    parse_script, it does not stop at the first. For editors and tests."""
    problems = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        try:
            parse(line)
        except QueryError as error:
            problems.append(str(QueryError(error.message, error.column, number)))
    return problems


def quote(text):
    """text as a token that tokenize reads back as the same text: a bare
    word when that is safe, otherwise a quoted string with escapes."""
    if text and text != "*" and not any(ch.isspace() or ch in '"\\' for ch in text):
        return text
    escaped = text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\t", "\\t")
    return f'"{escaped}"'


def format_command(command):
    """A Command as one line of the language; parse gives the same Command
    back. SCAN's open bounds (None) are written as a bare *."""
    words = [command.op]
    for arg in command.args:
        words.append("*" if arg is None else quote(arg))
    return " ".join(words)
--- hint
In `tokenize`, keep an index `i` and branch on `line[i]`: white space moves on; `"` starts an inner loop that collects characters into a list until the closing quote, handling `\` by looking at `line[i + 1]`; anything else reads a word. Record `start + 1` as each token's column.
--- hint
In `parse`, split the tokens into the first one and the rest, look the op up in `ARGUMENTS`, then compare `len(args)` with the number of names. Build the values in a loop over `zip(names, args)`, where the `SCAN` case and the empty-key case are two `if`s.
--- hint
`parse_script` and `lint` both loop over `enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1)`, skip the same lines, and catch `QueryError` from `parse`: one raises `QueryError(error.message, error.column, number)`, the other appends its `str`.

+++ practice | Tokens of a calculator
--- task
Write `calc_tokens(line)` that splits an arithmetic line into tokens `(kind, text, column)`: `"num"` for a run of digits, `"op"` for one of `+ - * / ( )`. Spaces separate tokens and are skipped. Columns count from 1. Any other character raises `ValueError` with the message `f"unexpected {ch!r} at column {col}"`.

For example, `calc_tokens("12 + 3*4")` is `[("num", "12", 1), ("op", "+", 4), ("num", "3", 6), ("op", "*", 7), ("num", "4", 8)]`.
--- starter
def calc_tokens(line):
    return [("num", t, 1) for t in line.split()]
--- solution
def calc_tokens(line):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(line):
        ch = line[i]
        if ch == " ":
            i += 1
        elif ch.isdigit():
            start = i
            while i < len(line) and line[i].isdigit():
                i += 1
            tokens.append(("num", line[start:i], start + 1))
        elif ch in "+-*/()":
            tokens.append(("op", ch, i + 1))
            i += 1
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unexpected {ch!r} at column {i + 1}")
    return tokens
--- hint
Walk the line with an index. A digit starts an inner loop that reads the whole number; an operator is a token of one character.
--- hint
Remember where a number starts, so its column is `start + 1`.
--- check case | The example from the task
calc_tokens("12 + 3*4")
=> [("num", "12", 1), ("op", "+", 4), ("num", "3", 6), ("op", "*", 7), ("num", "4", 8)]
--- check case | Parentheses and no spaces
calc_tokens("(1+22)/3")
=> [("op", "(", 1), ("num", "1", 2), ("op", "+", 3), ("num", "22", 4), ("op", ")", 6), ("op", "/", 7), ("num", "3", 8)]
--- check case | An empty line
calc_tokens("   ")
=> []
--- check test | A bad character raises ValueError naming its column
raises(ValueError, lambda: calc_tokens("1 + x")) and raises(ValueError, lambda: calc_tokens("7 %")) and raises(ValueError, lambda: calc_tokens("2.5"))

+++ practice | Splitting arguments with quotes
--- task
Write `split_args(line)` that splits a command line into a list of strings: words are separated by spaces, and a double-quoted part is one argument that may contain spaces (the quotes themselves are not part of it). There are no escapes in this format. A quote that is never closed raises `ValueError` with the message `f"unterminated quote at column {c}"`, where `c` is the column (from 1) of the opening quote.

For example, `split_args('copy "my file" out')` is `["copy", "my file", "out"]`, and `split_args('say ""')` is `["say", ""]`.
--- starter
def split_args(line):
    return line.split()
--- solution
def split_args(line):
    args = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(line):
        if line[i] == " ":
            i += 1
        elif line[i] == '"':
            end = line.find('"', i + 1)
            if end < 0:
                raise ValueError(f"unterminated quote at column {i + 1}")
            args.append(line[i + 1:end])
            i = end + 1
        else:
            start = i
            while i < len(line) and line[i] not in ' "':
                i += 1
            args.append(line[start:i])
    return args
--- hint
Handle three cases at the current position: a space, a quote, and the start of a word.
--- hint
For a quote, `line.find('"', i + 1)` finds the closing one, or returns -1 if there is none.
--- check case | The examples from the task
(split_args('copy "my file" out'), split_args('say ""'))
=> (["copy", "my file", "out"], ["say", ""])
--- check case | Extra spaces
split_args('   a    "b  c"   d ')
=> ["a", "b  c", "d"]
--- check case | Nothing to split
split_args("")
=> []
--- check test | An unterminated quote raises ValueError
raises(ValueError, lambda: split_args('open "log')) and split_args('x "y"') == ["x", "y"]

+++ practice | A table-driven rover language
--- task
A rover accepts three commands, in any case: `MOVE n` (n a whole number of metres, 1 to 100), `TURN direction` (`left` or `right`, in any case), and `STOP` (no arguments). Write `parse_rover(line)` that returns a tuple such as `("MOVE", 12)`, `("TURN", "left")` or `("STOP",)`, using a table from command to its argument check. Raise `ValueError` with these messages:

- `"empty command"` for a blank line;
- `f"unknown command {word!r}"`;
- `f"{op} takes {n} argument(s)"` when the number of arguments is wrong (n is 1 or 0);
- `f"bad argument {arg!r}"` when the argument is not allowed.
--- starter
def parse_rover(line):
    words = line.split()
    return tuple(words)
--- solution
def check_distance(arg):
    if arg.isdigit() and 1 <= int(arg) <= 100:
        return int(arg)
    raise ValueError(f"bad argument {arg!r}")


def check_direction(arg):
    if arg.lower() in ("left", "right"):
        return arg.lower()
    raise ValueError(f"bad argument {arg!r}")


COMMANDS = {"MOVE": [check_distance], "TURN": [check_direction], "STOP": []}


def parse_rover(line):
    words = line.split()
    if not words:
        raise ValueError("empty command")
    op = words[0].upper()
    if op not in COMMANDS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown command {words[0]!r}")
    checks = COMMANDS[op]
    if len(words) - 1 != len(checks):
        raise ValueError(f"{op} takes {len(checks)} argument(s)")
    return (op, *[check(arg) for check, arg in zip(checks, words[1:])])
--- hint
Make a dict from each command to a list of argument-checking functions: one function for `MOVE`, one for `TURN`, none for `STOP`.
--- hint
Look the command up, compare the number of arguments with the length of its list, then run each check on its argument.
--- check case | Good commands, in any case
[parse_rover(s) for s in ["MOVE 12", "turn LEFT", "Stop", "move 100"]]
=> [("MOVE", 12), ("TURN", "left"), ("STOP",), ("MOVE", 100)]
--- check test | Wrong argument counts
raises(ValueError, lambda: parse_rover("MOVE")) and raises(ValueError, lambda: parse_rover("STOP now")) and raises(ValueError, lambda: parse_rover("TURN left right"))
--- check test | Bad arguments, unknown commands and blank lines
all(raises(ValueError, lambda: parse_rover(s)) for s in ["MOVE 0", "MOVE 101", "MOVE -3", "MOVE 2.5", "TURN up", "FLY 3", "", "   "])

+++ practice | Turning escapes into characters
--- task
Write `unescape(text)` for the inside of a quoted string: `\"` becomes `"`, `\\` becomes `\`, `\n` a newline and `\t` a tab; every other character stays as it is. A backslash followed by any other character raises `ValueError` with the message `f"unknown escape at {i}"`, and a backslash at the very end raises `ValueError` with the message `f"lone backslash at {i}"`, where `i` is the backslash's index (from 0).

For example, `unescape('a\\tb')` (the characters a, backslash, t, b) is `"a\tb"`.
--- starter
def unescape(text):
    return text.replace("\\n", "\n").replace("\\t", "\t")
--- solution
ESCAPES = {'"': '"', "\\": "\\", "n": "\n", "t": "\t"}


def unescape(text):
    out = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(text):
        ch = text[i]
        if ch != "\\":
            out.append(ch)
            i += 1
            continue
        if i + 1 == len(text):
            raise ValueError(f"lone backslash at {i}")
        if text[i + 1] not in ESCAPES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown escape at {i}")
        out.append(ESCAPES[text[i + 1]])
        i += 2
    return "".join(out)
--- hint
Chained `replace` calls go wrong on `\\n` (a backslash, then an `n`): it is an escaped backslash followed by the letter n, not a newline. Walk the text one character at a time instead.
--- hint
On a backslash, look at the next character: it must exist and be one of four; append what it stands for and skip both.
--- check case | The four escapes
unescape('q\\"b\\\\n\\tt')
=> 'q"b\\n\tt'
--- check case | No escapes, and an empty string
(unescape("plain text"), unescape(""))
=> ("plain text", "")
--- check test | An escaped backslash before n is not a newline
unescape("\\\\n") == "\\n" and "\n" not in unescape("\\\\n")
--- check test | Unknown escapes and a lone backslash raise ValueError
raises(ValueError, lambda: unescape("a\\qb")) and raises(ValueError, lambda: unescape("end\\"))

def simple_tokens(line):
    tokens = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(line):
        if line[i] == " ":
            i += 1
        elif line[i] == '"':
            end = line.index('"', i + 1)
            tokens.append(("string", line[i + 1:end], i + 1))
            i = end + 1

            while i < len(line) and line[i] != " ":
                i += 1
            tokens.append(("word", line[start:i], start + 1))

--- hint
